For a binary `[n,k,≥d]_2` code, let `v=2^k`, `h=v/2`, and let `z` be the number of zero generator columns. The excess-weight Cayley matrix has eigenvalues `q_z=h(n-z)-d(v-1)` and `d-hμ(x)`. proof_markdown:
## Scope

No construction is claimed. The result is a finite nonexistence theorem for the inner codes supporting the strongest conditional composition routes.

## 1. Excess-weight Cayley cubic lemma

Let `C` be a binary linear `[n,k,≥d]_2` code with full-rank generator matrix. Put `V=F_2^k`, `v=|V|=2^k`, and `h=v/2`. Let `μ(x)` be the multiplicity of column `x∈V`, and put `z=μ(0)`.

For `a∈V`, let `w(a)` be the weight of the codeword indexed by `a`. Define

`θ(0)=0`, and `θ(a)=w(a)-d` for `a≠0`.

All values of `θ` are nonnegative integers. Form the symmetric Cayley matrix

`A_{u,t}=θ(u+t)`.

Every entry of `A` is nonnegative, so `tr(A^3)≥0`.

The characters of `V` diagonalize `A`. Direct orthogonality gives the eigenvalue

`q_z=h(n-z)-d(v-1)`

at the principal character, and

`d-hμ(x)`

at a nonprincipal character indexed by `x≠0`. Consequently

`tr(A^3)=q_z^3+Σ_{x≠0}(d-hμ(x))^3`. `(1)`

Assume `h>d` and `n-z≤v-1`, as in every application below. For `F(t)=(d-ht)^3` and every integer `t≥2`,

`F(t-1)+F(1)-F(t)-F(0)=3h^2(t-1)(ht-2d)>0`. `(2)`

Thus splitting a repeated nonzero column into multiplicities `t-1` and `1` at an unused nonzero position strictly increases the right side of (1). Repeating this operation shows

`tr(A^3)≤U_z:=q_z^3+(v-1-n+z)d^3+(n-z)(d-h)^3`. `(3)`

Therefore every such code must satisfy `U_z≥0`.

Zero columns can be deleted without changing dimension or distance. Hence Griesmer gives

`0≤z≤n-g_2(k,d)`. `(4)`

For the finite checks, define `Φ(x)=x^3-(x-h)^3`. Then

`U_{z+1}-U_z=Φ(d)-Φ(q_z)`. `(5)`

The function satisfies `Φ(d)=Φ(h-d)` and is strictly increasing above `h/2`. In each row below, the smallest allowed `q_z` exceeds `h-d`, so `U_z` strictly decreases with `z`. It therefore suffices to check `U_0`.

| `n` | `k` | excluded `d` | `g_2(k,d)` | `z_max` | `q_(z_max)` | `h-d` | `U_0` |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|8192|16|4088|8179|13|102392|28680|−41823326309449728|
|16384|16|8183|16369|15|106487|24585|−2674870102917120|
|16384|17|8182|16368|16|270326|57354|−734033369735626752|
|16384|18|8181|16368|16|794613|122891|−6091077791915704320|

Every displayed `U_0` is negative, contradicting (3). Hence

`d_max(8192,16)≤4087`,

`d_max(16384,16)≤8182`,

`d_max(16384,17)≤8181`,

`d_max(16384,18)≤8180`.

This proof permits arbitrary repeated and zero columns. It therefore supersedes restrictions merely requiring the proposed core to be nonprojective or non-antipodal.

## 2. Composition consequences

The proposed exceptional-line construction requires an `[8192,16,4092]_2` core, contradicting the first ceiling. Thus its conditional dimension-1041 target code does not exist.

The prior ordinary-RS sieve leaves only length-16384 inner dimensions 16, 17, and 18 as possible improvements over 1040. The new ceilings require respective outer distances

`ceil(D/8182)=65488`,

`ceil(D/8181)=65496`,

`ceil(D/8180)=65504`.

For outer length 65536, Singleton gives outer dimensions at most 49, 41, and 33. The corresponding binary dimensions are 784, 697, and 594. Hence none improves 1040, and the previously conditional `[16384,17,8188]_2` dimension-1649 route is impossible.

## 3. Common-kernel covering lemma

Retain the upstream two-fiber notation: `B_s:F_2^K→F_2^16`, `e_0=(1,0,…,0)`, and

`Δ(x)=Σ_s(1_{B_sx=0}-1_{B_sx=e_0})≤64` for every `x≠0`.

Choose any 65 seeds `T` and put `Q=∩_{s∈T}ker B_s`, `q=dim Q`. If `r_s=rank(B_s|Q)`, exact fiber counting gives

`Σ_{x∈Q}Δ(x)=Σ_{s:e_0∉B_s(Q)}2^(q-r_s)`. `(6)`

Because `Δ(0)=32768`, the left side is at most

`32768+64(2^q-1)=64·2^q+32704`. `(7)`

The 65 seeds in `T` contribute `65·2^q`. Let `M` count outside seeds for which `e_0∉B_s(Q)`. Every such seed contributes at least one more unit, so

`65·2^q+M≤64·2^q+32704`.

Thus `q≤14`, `M≤32704-2^q`, and among the 32703 outside seeds at least

`32703-M≥2^q-1` `(8)`

satisfy `e_0∈B_s(Q)`. Moreover, for each nonzero `x∈Q`, the 65 killed fibers give `z_0(x)≥65`; the target inequality forces `z_1(x)≥1`. Hence those outside affine fibers cover every nonzero point of `Q`.

At `K=1054`, upstream rank rigidity gives `q=14` for every 65-set, so at least 16383 outside seeds hit `e_0` on each common kernel.

## 4. Residual endpoint audit

The published source proving `N_2(9,32)=70` also displays a `[71,10,32]` code and a full-length `[70,9,32]` subcode. Thus both terminal residual endpoints exist; searching for their nonexistence would not close the route. The cubic argument instead rules out the required inverse lifts directly.

Character orthogonality gives the exact eigenvalues, and the positive splitting identity shows that distinct nonzero generator columns maximize the cubic trace at fixed zero-column count.

theorem_statement: The excess-weight Cayley cubic lemma proves `d_max(8192,16)≤4087`, `d_max(16384,16)≤8182`, `d_max(16384,17)≤8181`, and `d_max(16384,18)≤8180`. Therefore the conditional `[8192,16,4092]_2` exceptional-line core, `[16384,16,8185]_2` gateway, and `[16384,17,8188]_2` gateway are all nonexistent. Combined with the durable finite sieve, this closes every ordinary Reed–Solomon/product-distance composition above dimension 1040. Separately, every 65-fold common kernel in a standard two-fiber family is covered on all nonzero points by at least `2^q-1` outside `e_0`-fibers; at `K=1054` this means at least 16383 outside seeds.
title: Cubic excess-weight obstruction eliminates the 1041 core and the 1649 ordinary-RS gateway
